textbookText: Pipette Pipettes are long narrow tubes having a bulb in the middle. The upper stem of the pipette has a mark upto which it is to be filled with solution• Pipettes are of different capacities i.e. 50, 25, 20, 10 and 5 ml. Before using' the pipette should be thoroughly washed with distilled water and then rinsed with the solution that is to be pipetted out. While introducing the pipetted out solution into the titration flask, the pipette should not be blown in.

Volumetric flask A volumetric flask is a pear shaped vessel with a long narrow neck and having a lid. A mark is made around the neck to indicate a definite volume i.e. 1000, 500, 200 or 100 ml. This flask is used to prepare primary standard solution and for diluting a solution to a definite volume. Before using, the flask and the lid should be thoroughly washed distilled water.

Volumetric Analysis Conical flask It is also called titration flask. Generally, a 250 ml conical flask is used as a titration flask in laboratory. Titration has to be done in this flask. Before using, the flask should be thoroughly washed with distilled water. It should never be rinsed otherwise the volume of the solution by which it's rinsed will not be accurate.

During titration, the conicai flask should be shaken continuously with clockwise rotation while putting the solution from the burette dropwisely. The solution should not splash. Hold the neck of the conical flask with your right hand and stop cock of the burette with your left hand as shown in figure below. As soon as the end point is noticed, close the stop cock immediately. 20 c A 500-mil. litre measuring flask Pipette Burette Conical flask Figure 4.1: Apparatus used in titration

100 Chemistry Points to be followed in titration Do not touch the solution in the conical flask by the glass tube while adding the indicator or any other solution (like acid) with the help of this tube.
Do not add excess of indicator. Do not introduce the solution from the burette on the wall of the conical flask. Do not splash the solution in the conical flask.
Rough reading can be taken at the first time to minimize the time.
A white paper can be placed below the conical flask if you get confused in predicüng the colour change while predicting the end point.

Take the reading by keeping your eyes in the same line with the level of the solution. Lower meniscus of the colourless soluüons should coincide the mark of the pipette, burette or volumetric flask to avoid parallax and due to which, the volume noted will be accurate. Take the reading corresponding to the lowest point of the cup-shaped surface. Similarly, for the coloured solutions, their upper meniscus should coincide the mark of these apparatus.
There should not be any air bubbles into the pipette and burette containing the solutions.
During titration, usually more corrosive solutions are taken into the burette.
Before using, check whether the stop cock of the burette funcüons well.
Clamp the burette to the stand vertically straight. Care should be taken so that the breakage does not occur during clamping.

Do not blow out the last drop of the solution of the pipette into the conical flask. At last, just touch the tip of the pipette slightly on the empty space on the base of the conical flask. The last portion of the solution which remains in the tip of the pipette should not be fransferred by jerk or any other ways.
